title: When Features Beat Noise: A Noise-Driven Hypothesis Testing Method for Feature Selection
abstract: arXiv:2511.20851v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Feature selection has remained a daunting challenge in machine learning and artificial intelligence, where increasingly complex, high-dimensional datasets demand principled strategies for isolating the most informative predictors. Despite widespread adoption, many established techniques such as Boruta, Recursive Feature Elimination and other wrapper based methods suffer from notable limitations; some incur substantial computational cost, while others offer no definite statistical driven stopping criteria or assess the significance of their importance scores. This paper proposes a novel feature selection method that addresses these limitations. Our approach introduces multiple random noise features and evaluates each feature's importance against the maximum importance value among these noise features incorporating a non-parametric bootstrap-based hypothesis testing framework to establish a solid theoretical foundation. translated_title: 当特征战胜噪声：一种噪声驱动的假设检验特征选择方法
translated_abstract: 特征选择一直是机器学习和人工智能领域的一项艰巨挑战，日益复杂的高维数据集需要有原则性的策略来筛选出信息量最大的预测变量。尽管被广泛采用，许多成熟的技术（如Boruta、递归特征消除以及其他基于封装器的方法）都存在明显的局限性：有些方法计算成本高昂，而另一些方法则缺乏明确的统计驱动的停止准则，或无法评估其重要性分数的显著性。本文提出了一种新颖的特征选择方法来解决这些局限。我们的方法引入多个随机噪声特征，并将每个真实特征的重要性与这些噪声特征中的最大重要性值进行比较，同时结合基于非参数bootstrap的假设检验框架，以建立坚实的理论基础。我们建立……
tldr: 本文提出一种噪声驱动的特征选择方法，通过将每个特征的重要性与随机噪声特征中的最大重要性进行基于非参数bootstrap的假设检验，为特征选择提供了坚实的统计理论基础和显著性评估准则。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a noise-driven feature selection method that evaluates each feature's importance against the maximum importance among random noise features within a non-parametric bootstrap-based hypothesis testing framework, providing a statistically grounded criterion for feature significance assessment.
